Chapter 8: The Upside-Down Kingdom in a World of Empire
When you look at history, it’s almost always shaped by empires—these huge systems built around power, control, and the promise of safety.
Think about the Roman Empire back in the teacher’s day, or the economic and political giants that dominate the world now. The logic is pretty familiar: keep climbing that ladder, protect your own, and make sure no one threatens your spot.
But here’s where the upside-down kingdom turns everything on its head.
It’s not about taking down empires with more force. Instead, it undermines them with something much more radical—love.
Living this way reveals just how empty power can be, and how violence never really gets us what we hope for.
Picture this: a group of friends in a small apartment, surrounded by reminders of a broken world—news about war, stories of injustice, the everyday stress of trying to make ends meet.
They’re reading the teacher’s words, wondering how on earth they’re supposed to live them out right now.
It’s tempting to just retreat, to focus on their own spiritual lives and let the world sort itself out. But the upside-down kingdom doesn’t really let them off that easy.
They start noticing all the subtle ways empire shapes their lives—the pressure to succeed, the fear that there’s never enough, the way we’re quietly taught to see others as threats.
It’s pretty uncomfortable, but it opens their eyes. Suddenly, they’re asking new kinds of questions. Who’s being left out? Whose voices aren’t being heard? And what if they used what they have—not just for themselves, but for the good of others?
One friend decides to use her skills to speak up for people who don’t have a voice. Another chooses a simpler way of living, freeing up extra time and money to help those in need.
Their choices aren’t making the news, but they’re making a difference—little ripples that challenge what people assume is just the way things are.
The upside-down kingdom isn’t about running away from the world. It’s about changing it from the inside out.
It’s about living honestly, refusing to play by empire’s rules, and believing that even the smallest acts of faithfulness can actually shift the world around us.
Maybe you’ve felt powerless in the face of injustice. Most of us have. But here’s the reminder: real power isn’t found in dominating others. It’s found in love.
The invitation is this—resist the pull of empire. Not with anger or despair, but with hope, and with courage.
